History of the Huron County Circuit Court

The Huron County Circuit Court was established in 1873, after Huron County was separated from Sanilac County. The court initially had only one judge, but as the county grew, additional judges were added. Today, the court has three judges, who are elected to six-year terms by the voters of Huron County.

Over the years, the Huron County Circuit Court has played a critical role in shaping the legal landscape of the region. Many landmark cases have been heard in this court, and its decisions have had far-reaching effects on the lives of residents and businesses in Huron County.

Jurisdiction and Functions of the Huron County Circuit Court

The Huron County Circuit Court is a trial court with general jurisdiction, which means that it has the power to hear and decide all types of cases that are brought before it. The court has the authority to hear cases involving civil, criminal, and family law matters.

In addition to its trial court function, the Huron County Circuit Court also has limited appellate jurisdiction, which means that it can hear appeals from certain lower courts in Huron County.

The Huron County Circuit Court hears a wide range of cases, including but not limited to:
